speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To understand your infant's recurrent stridor and wheezing, I need to ask: At what age did these symptoms first begin, and do they occur specifically when the baby is feeding or crying?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngotracheomalacia. The clinical presentation of inspiratory stridor exacerbated by crying, feeding, and specifically neck flexion in a 10-month-old, accompanied by feeding difficulties and vomiting, is highly characteristic of this condition. Given the clear diagnostic picture, I will now request a neck flexion lateral neck X-ray and a flexible nasolaryngoscopy to confirm the tracheal collapse.
